name: Hook-Ladder Mesh with TE Stack (Quick Deception Screen)
formation: 11P Gun Trips Left vs Nickel Under

summary.motive: Exploit man-coverage rules with a 2-man mesh rub that legally frees the RB against press-man Nickel coverage on 3rd down.
summary.whyItWorks: In man coverage, the TE's hook route creates a legal and physical pick that the WILL linebacker cannot follow through; the RB slips free into the flat with a full step of separation by the time the QB delivers.
summary.failureMode: A zone-coverage call that removes man assignments; in zone the hook/ladder becomes predictable and the curl-flat defender can collision both TE and RB.

beats.title: 1. Two-Man Mesh Concept
beats.text: TE runs a 5-yard hook while the RB releases from the backfield on the "ladder" — the classic 2-man mesh where the second receiver (RB) slips past the first receiver's (TE) hook to create a natural pick.

beats.title: 2. The Rub and Slip
beats.text: The WILL linebacker is in man coverage on the RB but cannot follow him through the natural rub that the TE's hook creates. The RB slips free with a full stride of separation as the WILL crashes into the TE body.

beats.title: 3. Lateral in Space
beats.text: The QB flips a quick lateral pass to the RB running free in space. Nickel is dragged across the field by H's drag, MIKE is too deep inside, leaving a wide-open throwing lane and clear space for the RB to work in.

beats.title: 4. First Down in Space
beats.text: The RB catches in space 8 yards beyond the LOS with only the free safety to beat. The hook-ladder deception has converted a critical third-and-5 by exploiting man-coverage rubs.

relations.tell: TE aligned tight to line at tackle depth; RB initial release toward TE before sharp angle to mesh.
